paper_metadata.title: Alternative pipeline for option pricing using quantum computers

summary: The paper proposes a new quantum Monte Carlo pipeline combining a direct payoff encoding with a modified real quantum amplitude estimation (mRQAE) algorithm to price derivatives with negative payoffs. Simulated experiments on an Atos QLM emulator (≈5–10 qubits) show convergence behavior comparable to standard QAMC methods while theoretically retaining the quadratic Monte Carlo speedup (O(1/ϵ) vs O(1/ϵ²)).

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo option-pricing experiments using square-root encoding and modified iterative quantum amplitude estimation (mIQAE) on positive-payoff contracts.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) with square-root encoding and mIQAE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ϵ and confidence 1-γ in amplitude estimation

hyperparameters.precision_levels: multiple ϵ values shown in Fig. 6

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Black-Scholes path distribution encoded into a quantum state; square-root encoding loads sqrt(payoff) into an ancilla amplitude
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[F(ST)|Ft] for option payoffs under Black-Scholes dynamics

problem_instance.description: Vanilla call, digital call, vanilla put, digital put, and linear payoff options under Black-Scholes terminal-price simulation

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic Black-Scholes terminal distribution discretized on 32 points between 0.01 and 5.0

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Exact Black-Scholes simulation with risk-neutral rate 0.01 and volatility 0.5; one-year maturity; initial price 1.0
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Absolute error versus discretized expectation plotted against number of oracle calls; medians and 25th/75th percentiles over repeated runs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Black-Scholes distribution discretization; exact one-step simulation instead of multi-step SDE discretization
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated zero-state probability to option price using normalization constants

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: absolute error decreases with oracle calls; medians and interquartile ranges reported

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation and the same oracle cost model
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup in query complexity; experiments are on a quantum emulator, not real hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/ϵ) oracle calls for amplitude estimation

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not quantified; theoretical quadratic scaling O(1/ϵ) vs classical O(1/ϵ²)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Hundreds to thousands of logical qubits for realistic path discretizations and deep Grover-style circuits with many oracle calls
limiting_factors: State preparation oracle for probability distributions is expensive
Amplitude estimation requires deep Grover-style circuits
Current hardware lacks required logical qubit counts
Quadratic speedup only; constant factors and fault-tolerance overhead dominate

5 qubits inferred from the paper's statement that 32 discretization points require 5 qubits.
